job.style: a short story where children solve a real problem

response.passage: Rohan and his friends decided to survey the heights of all students in their school to create a fitness report. They collected the raw data directly by measuring each student with a tape, ensuring it was primary data. To organize the numbers, they created continuous class intervals like 140-150 cm and 150-160 cm, carefully placing a student who is exactly 150 cm tall into the 150-160 cm group to avoid overlap. After listing the frequencies, they calculated the cumulative frequency by adding each class frequency to the sum of all previous ones. To visualize the distribution, they drew a histogram where the bars touch each other because the data is continuous. Finally, they drew a frequency polygon by joining the midpoints of the tops of the histogram bars, extending the line to touch the horizontal axis at the midpoints of the classes immediately before the first and after the last class. When calculating the median height for their group of 21 students, they first arranged the heights in ascending order and identified the 11th value as the middle observation. They concluded that the median is the middle value of the ordered list, not just the middle class by position.
response.summary: Rohan's team collected primary data on student heights and organized it into continuous class intervals. They used histograms and frequency polygons to represent the data and correctly identified the median from ordered observations.
